# King's College London: Summary
King's College London, established in 1829, is one of the UK's leading research universities and a founding member of the University of London. With nine academic faculties, including arts and humanities, law, natural sciences, medicine, nursing, psychiatry, social sciences, and business, King's is recognized for its broad subject range and pioneering research. Its notable contributions include the discovery of the structure of DNA by Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin. The university has merged with several medical and dental schools, becoming Europe's largest center for healthcare education. King's was a founding member of the Russell Group and is part of the "golden triangle" of premier UK universities. It maintains active partnerships, such as King's Health Partners and the Francis Crick Institute, and has collaborations with leading institutions worldwide.
King's has five campuses in central London, with the main facilities at the Strand, Waterloo, Guy's, St Thomas', and Denmark Hill. The Maughan Library is its largest and houses extensive special collections. The university offers a rich student life, providing numerous clubs, societies, and sports, with an active students' union. King's consistently ranks among the top global universities (#31 QS, #36 THE in 2024/25) and is highly rated for graduate employability and research excellence. Its distinguished alumni include Nobel laureates, scientists, authors, and global leaders. King's academic dress is designed by Vivienne Westwood, and its historic buildings and museums feature in several films and television productions.
